The various branches of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set} employ their own forms of blood magic, each with a strongly religious character rooted in the trappings of a particular faith rather than the mechanical, intellectual style of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Thaumaturgy. These traditions use the Path system exactly like standard Thaumaturgy (an Intelligence + Occult roll for rituals, a Willpower roll for Path effects), but reflavor the Paths and rename them according to each tradition's own mythology. No new Paths or rituals with unique mechanics are introduced; Storytellers should use the existing Path rules from the appropriate sourcebooks (Vampire: the Masquerade Revised Edition, Guide to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, Guide to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}, and Blood Magic) with the renamed flavor below.

Setite Sorcery: Akhu

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set} themselves combine perverted funerary ritual, alchemy and classic Egyptian image-and-incantation magic. Most Setite rituals must be performed in a ritual chamber containing a cadaver stolen from a grave and mutilated according to instructions in the clan's holy book, The Book of Going Forth by Night; the Setites believe the desecrated corpse drains magical power from the Western Lands of Osiris. This is why the Setites call their own sorcery akhu ("the magic of the dead"), distinguishing it from heka, the magic used by mortals.

Common Akhu Paths include Corruption, the Snake Inside and the Dry Nile (used to detach mortals from their past lives), and historically Weather Control (Set being a storm god). Other Setite Paths include Spirit Manipulation (to evoke spirits of the Egyptian underworld) and Conjuring (to offer people their heart's desire, for a time). A few Warrior Setites learn the Path of Mars, which they call the Valor of Sutekh, claiming the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s version is an imitation of their own millennia-old tradition.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.Ohsrh5ieQL7q3Ewk]{Serpents of the Light}: Wanga

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.Ohsrh5ieQL7q3Ewk]{Serpents of the Light} draw their inspiration from Afro-Caribbean folk magic (chiefly Haitian Voudon and Cuban Palo Mayombe). Their general term for their sorcery is Wanga; individual spells may also be called Bilongo, Ebbo or Malice, and amulets/talismans are called Paquets Congo or Hands. A practitioner employs herbs, spices, powders, rum, candles, rattles, drumming, flour designs called Vevers, and blood sacrifice to appease the loa. Cobra sorcery has a strong necromantic cast: a Wangateur carries a Kisengue (a human shinbone wrapped in black rags) rather than an Egyptian priest's staff, and many rites use a Nganga, a cauldron of blood, graveyard dirt, bones, iron spikes and blades. Many Cobra sorcerers actually study Necromancy rather than Thaumaturgy, and use the term Wanga to cover both.

Spirit Manipulation is by far the most popular Path among Serpents of the Light; those who practice true Necromancy favor the Sepulchre Path almost exclusively. Wangateurs remember the old Setite Paths of Corruption, the Dry Nile and the Serpent Within under new names: the Dry Nile becomes Blinding Chango, and the Serpent Within becomes Zarabanda's Malice. Cobras especially value these three Paths for cursing their enemies.

Daitya Sadhana

The Daitya call their magic Sadhana ("magical arts"); a practitioner is a Sadhu, Paths are called Siddhi ("Attainments") and rituals are Tantras ("Instructions"). Some Siddhi duplicate familiar Paths under new names: Movement of the Mind reflects psychic mind-over-matter, Conjuring shows mastery through creating objects or living things by will, and Spirit Manipulation lets a Daitya contact and command her demonic cousins in other worlds. The Daitya also possess several Paths unique to themselves that mirror Hindu legend: knowledge of past and future, control of destiny, assuming other forms, instantaneous travel and more (left to the Storyteller to adjudicate using comparable existing Path effects, as no separate mechanics are given).

A Sadhu must engage in long meditation and grueling austerities to unlock the Blood's mystic power: fasting nearly to torpor, yogic and breathing exercises, and exposure to heat, cold and other unpleasantness. Rituals incorporate yantras (mystic symbols), mantras (mystic syllables or phrases), mandalas (complex drawings), mudras (ritual gestures) and sacrifices of blood, butter and soma (an intoxicating plant-derived liquid). Sadhana rituals always demand sacrifice by fire.

Tlacique Nahuallotl

The Tlacique call their blood magic Nahuallotl; a practitioner is a Nahualli. The Tlacique lost most of their magic in their defeat by the Sabbat, and fewer than a dozen of their blood magicians survive into the modern nights. Surviving Paths work exactly like @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Paths (a Willpower roll for Path powers, an Intelligence + Occult roll for rituals). The Tlacique independently created the Path of Blood and all their magicians begin with it as their primary Path.

Most Nahuallotl Paths bear the names of gods: Weather Control becomes the Breath of Quetzalcoatl, the Path of Corruption becomes the Secret Ways of Tezcatlipoca, the Path of Blood becomes the Flower of the Divine Liquor (Huehueteotl's Glory), and Spirit Manipulation becomes the Rites of Tezcatlipoca. Nahuallotl always involves sacrifice: while expending power from his own blood and praying for the appropriate god's aid, a Nahualli sheds a token offering of vitae from the tongue, earlobe or genitals, traditionally drawn with a large cactus spine carried for the purpose. Every ritual beyond level 5 requires the sacrifice of an animal's or a human's life, though few such rituals survive to the modern nights.

Cult Leadership and Divine Power

The Setites' clan Disciplines — Obfuscate and Presence, alongside their signature Serpentis — are especially suited to playing the role of a living god before a mortal blood cult. Presence supplies awe, dread and a supernatural call; Obfuscate lets a Setite walk unseen among mortals to learn their secrets, or take on the appearance of a god outright (often aided by simple props such as an animal-headed mask, which Mask of a Thousand Faces then renders convincing). Serpentis is more limited in this role: transforming into a snake-man or giant serpent impresses onlookers but leaves few options for varied divine impersonation, so Setite priests mostly reserve Skin of the Adder for portraying Set himself. Eyes of the Serpent can emulate Presence in a limited way, catching a mortal's eye with a magnetic gaze so that fascination with the vampire's eyes is mistaken for fascination with her message.

Setites do not restrict themselves to their clan Disciplines for this purpose: Warrior Setites use a small display of crushing strength to cow uncooperative mortals, and old tradition recommends Animalism to assert divinity quietly by making beasts fawn at the vampire's feet. Above all, Setite Thaumaturgy (Akhu, Wanga, Sadhana or Nahuallotl, as above) offers a wealth of ways to bless, curse and bedazzle Kindred and kine alike, reinforcing a Setite priest's claim to divinity.

A Setite who ruthlessly exploits a blood cult as a Herd while giving nothing back is scornfully called an "Osiris" by the clan, after the greedy, deluding methods Setites ascribe to their hated enemy; other vampires have since borrowed the term for any similarly parasitic cult leader. A Setite who behaves this way loses @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.St7uVm2DqK4nRy8X]{Status} among more devout clanmates, who may refuse to associate with her or actively make trouble for her with other local Kindred.
